intent: Name what is missing in a short headline.
typical_uses: The one-line headline of an Empty, such as "No results"

dont_use_when.situation: The title of a card that holds real content

invariants.text: Without `render` EmptyTitle renders a div with no heading role or level, so it does not appear in the page's heading outline; `render={<h2 />}` (any heading level) puts it there, keeping the title class and resetting the UA heading margins and font at zero specificity.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep EmptyTitle to the short headline and give the explanation its own EmptyDescription beneath it

render.states: render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (EmptyTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h2 />}`.

good.title: A headline in the page outline

bad.title: The explanation folded into the headline
bad.code:
<EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyTitle>No results. Try a different search term or clear your filters.</EmptyTitle>
</EmptyHeader>
bad.why: EmptyTitle is the headline; the explanation belongs in EmptyDescription, which carries the muted body text.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (EmptyTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h2 />}`.
